 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 6.10.2010 passed by Tenth Additional MACT, (Fast Track) District-Gwalior (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.62/2010 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation and also aggrieved by the finding of the Tribunal by which Tribunal Exonerated Insurance Company from liability.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of injury of the claimant, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.4000/- has been awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17241 2 MA-378-2011 by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant filed this appeal on the ground that Tribunal has committed error in passing the award.
The award is manifestly illegal and against settled principles of law.
Tribunal has not considered the evidence available on record and not awarded compensation under the head of disability and other heads.

It is further submitted that at the time of accident, driver of Naresh vs Banti Rathore on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118333521/
1 the offending vehicle has carried driving license of light motor vehicle (LMV) and weight of the alleged vehicle is less than 7500 Kg.

sentences.text: So, there is no need of endorsement and prayed for setting aside the finding of the Claims Tribunal in this regard and submitted that Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supported the impugned award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the entire record.
7. It is undisputed that at the time of accident driver of the offending vehicle has carried driving license of light motor vehicle and alleged vehicle was Mahindra Pick up which weighed less than 7500 Kg.
8.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. AIR 2017 SC 3668, the Apex Court held that:-
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg, would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2) (d)
is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:17241 3 MA-378-2011 vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is to say; no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.

A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form."
9.

In view of the aforesaid , it is clear that when the weight of the vehicle is below 7500 Kg and driver of the offending vehicle has LMV license, then no need to separate endorsement of license is required to drive transport vehicle.
So, from the aforesaid discussion, it is clear that Tribunal has given wrong finding and committed error in totally exonerating the Insurance Company.
So, finding of the Tribunal in this regard is set aside.
Accordingly Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation to the claimant jointly and severally with owner and driver of the alleged vehicle.
Insurance Company is firstly liable.

10. On the point of enhancement, considering the injury, age of the claimant and other circumstances, it shall be appropriate to enhance the award amount to the extent of Rs. 15,000/-
11.
The appellant/claimant is entitled to receive Rs.15000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
